content: The Island Medical Program (IMP) at the University of Victoria was established by the provincial government to address the need for more physicians on Vancouver Island in British Columbia. This program is part of the University of British Columbia's (UBC) Faculty of Medicine and was launched in September 2004 in collaboration with the University of Northern British Columbia (UNBC), the University of Victoria (UVic), and the provincial government. It is an innovative, distributed medical education program. Medical training in British Columbia is now distributed across three sites: the Island Medical Program (IMP) at UVic, the Northern Medical Program (NMP) at UNBC, and the Vancouver-Fraser Medical Program (VFMP) at UBC. An additional site, the Okanagan Medical Program (OMP), was planned to begin in 2009, adding 30 seats to UBC's medical class. Students in the IMP are based in the Medical Sciences Building at UVic. All students across the three sites (IMP, NMP, and VFMP) follow the same curriculum and are connected through advanced audiovisual and e-learning technologies, enabling simultaneous and interactive learning. IMP students are fully registered with the UBC Faculty of Medicine and will receive UBC degrees. While at UVic, they hold affiliate status, granting them access to all services available to UVic students. IMP students spend the first four months of their undergraduate medical program at UBC in Vancouver before relocating to Victoria to complete their degree requirements. During the third and fourth years, which are more clinically focused, students gain extensive experience in hospital and community-based clinical settings within the Vancouver Island Health Authority. Upon completing the four-year MD undergraduate program, graduates enter residency training across Canada and internationally in one of over 50 specialty areas. Post-graduate training durations range from two to six years. Applications for the Island Medical Program are processed through the UBC MD Undergraduate Program Admissions office. Currently, 24 students are admitted to the IMP annually. The IMP is linked with other health science programs offered at the University of Victoria, including Nursing, Social Work, Psychology, Health Information Science, the Centre on Aging, the Centre for Addictions Research of British Columbia, and the Centre for Biomedical Research. The program consists of four years of study: Years 1 and 2: General sciences or Foundations of Medicine. During the first term, IMP and NMP students attend classes at UBC's Vancouver campus alongside VFMP students. Years 3 and 4: Clinical training. Year 4 includes advanced clerkship, residency preparation, and participation in the Canadian Resident Matching Service (CaRMS). Notable alumni of the program include: Mark Lipsett: Made significant advances in diabetes research. Jamie Loh: Developed the smallpox vaccine. Brian Yong: Advocated for the use of the digital rectal examination (DRE) technique for detecting benign prostatic hyperplasia. Jeff Campbell: Developed the acid-fast stain. Angela Lin: First identified schistocytes in microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. Chelsea Greenwood: Contributed to the development of hybrid car technology. JJ Hamilton: Known as a Jedi Master.
